label: prf:unified-iterative-correction
title: Proof of unified iterative correction
html:
Proof. Proof of unified iterative correction

Proof. By prop:mass-coefficient-shadow-price, the BW coefficient of partition \lambda is the LP-dual variable u_\lambda^* = C_\lambda \cdot S_\lambda(Z, N, A). The categorical scale C_\lambda = m_e \cdot H_q(\lambda) (the q-hook product over the Young diagram of \lambda) is the universal constant determined by the partition algebra, with no nuclear data; the scaling function S_\lambda(Z, N, A) is realised at each step as \ln|\mathrm{tr}\,\mathbf{M}_\lambda^{(0..A)}| - \ln d_\lambda via the Young seminormal representation.

For \lambda = (2,2) \vdash 4 this recovers the dedicated Wigner identity (prop:wigner-np-pairing): H_q((2,2)) = [3]_q \cdot [2]_q^2; for \lambda = (2,1) \vdash 3 it reproduces the volume / surface / Coulomb decomposition through their image under the Wedderburn embedding — a step this proof does not discharge, and which the corpus still cannot supply.

Updated 2026-09-05 (bean qou-kp2z). Bean qou-qb7p gave three reasons the corpus could not supply this step. Two of them have since been removed and one has not, so the clause remains an open obligation for a narrower reason than before. Removed: the only formalised embedding was QOU.HeckeAlgebra.Wedderburn.wedderburnEmbed, declared opaque ("keeps the embedding opaque pending concrete construction") and registering as a fourth axiom beside propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound in any #print axioms that reached it. It is now a real construction — QOU.HeckeAlgebra.Wedderburn.blockDiagonal, with footprint exactly those three — and the opaque has been deleted. Not removed, and decisive here: the shape objection is untouched. The constructed map has the same type \bigoplus_\lambda M_{f^\lambda} \to M_{n!}, assembling blocks into one matrix rather than splitting one block's scalar C_{(2,1)} into three coefficients; building it changed its status, not its direction or its arity. The landing in M_{n!} is additionally conditional on the RSK identity \sum_\lambda (f^\lambda)^2 = n!, carried as the named hypothesis RSKDimIdentity and discharged by nothing here.

That objection is now a theorem, not a remark (QOU/HeckeAlgebra/WedderburnTrace.lean). The naive form — "three independent coefficients cannot come from one scalar" — is false, since one real encodes three set-theoretically. Under linearity, which this corpus already assumes for the Markov trace, it is true: that trace factors through the block traces, so a functional of that form supported at a single \lambda is exactly c_\lambda \cdot \operatorname{tr}(x_\lambda) — one coefficient against one number — and any three such are linearly dependent, with an explicit witness (three_supported_traceFunctionals_dependent).

This does not make the clause false; it rules out the route the clause names, whenever that route is linear, factors through the Markov trace, and is localised at (2,1). It also says where the room is, which is the more useful half: f^{(2,1)} = 2, so the block is M_2(\mathbb{R}) — four real dimensions, of which the trace reads one. The information wanted is present in the block and destroyed by tracing it — itself now a theorem (trace_does_not_separate, exists_indistinguishable_by_every_traceFunctional): whenever a block has dimension at least 2 there are distinct decompositions on which every block trace agrees, so every trace-factoring functional, the Markov trace included, takes the same value on both. Instantiating that at (2,1) needs f^{(2,1)} = 2; that value is now formalised (SeminormalDimSmall.seminormalDim_p21, via the Frame–Robinson–Thrall hook-length formula), so trace_does_not_separate_p21 holds unconditionally. The general theorems keep the bound as a hypothesis because they are about any block of dimension \geq 2. The boundary is real: f^{(1,1)} = 1, so at the charge shape the block is its trace and none of this applies. A derivation reading the block rather than its trace is not blocked by any of this — and that is now constructive rather than merely permitted: three_blockEntry_independent_p21 exhibits three linearly independent block-reading functionals at (2,1), the exact complement of the three trace-factoring ones being dependent. It does not identify those three with volume, surface and Coulomb; three independent functionals existing is a necessary condition for such a match, not evidence of one. So the clause is still an open obligation, not a derivation; for higher partitions it adds the form-factor, pn-correlation, and {[3,2,1]} pn-invisible corrections.

By the Markov-trace normalization (the per-level budget is the Hecke-level scale [k]_q!, k fixed), the dual shadow prices satisfy a single budget constraint per Hecke level; by Frobenius reciprocity (prop:mass-coefficient-shadow-price, branching corollary), shadow prices at level k+1 are determined by those at level k. Telescoping per-step log-trace differences across k = 1, \ldots, A yields the closed-form B_\lambda.

The Kerov q-hook walk [kerov1996] gives the iterative Markov-chain interpretation of \mathrm{tr}\,\mathbf{M}_\lambda^{(0..k)} as a transition kernel on the Young lattice; the Féray–Méliot q-Plancherel CLT [feray-meliot2012] guarantees the asymptotic convergence of the accumulator at rate O(1/\sqrt{A}) across Hecke levels.

The three legacy mechanisms specialise:

  • deuteron (A = 2, dedicated \alpha_{\mathrm{Borromean}} \cdot \hat V_e): the A = 2 slice of the LP-dual accumulator, dominated by the (2,1) and (2,2) shadow prices;
  • knot factor (A = 3, 4, dedicated a(N) = 1 - h^2, (1 - h^2)^2): the A = 3, 4 slices of the LP-dual accumulator, where the (2,1) and (3,1) contributions reproduce the figure-eight and Borromean amphicheiral factors;
  • Wigner energy (k = 4, dedicated -\Delta_W \cdot T(T+1)/A): the k = 4 self-conjugate shadow price \lambda = (2,2), which vanishes on isolated pn crossings (extremal cancellation, prop:confined-knot-binding) but is nonzero on collective pn patterns. Under convention D no self-conjugate partition beyond k = 4 can contribute: self-conjugacy forces \ell(\lambda) = \lambda_1, so the row cap \ell(\lambda) \leq 2 admits only (1), (2,1) and (2,2), and a block with \tilde w_\lambda = 0 has C_\lambda = 0 and hence u_\lambda^* = 0 at every (Z, N) — the vanishing is upstream of the scaling function, so no S_\lambda restores it.

\square

Algorithm summary (one block, no special cases, A = 1 onward):

for k in 2..K_PARTITION_MAX:
  for partition λ of k:
    H_q(λ)   = ∏_{x∈λ} [h_x]_q
    d_λ      = #SYT(λ)
    w_λ      = d_q(λ)^2 / [k]_q!
    y_λ      = w_λ / d_λ − 1/[k]_q!
    σ_1..σ_{k−1} = YSN matrices in λ
for step = 1..A:
  for each partition λ:
    M_λ      ← M_λ × ∏(c*σ_g + d*I) over new crossings at this step
    ΔB_λ     = m_e * H_q(λ) * y_λ * (ln|Tr M_λ| − previous)
    cumulative_λ += ΔB_λ
    record witness row
B_unified = Σ_λ cumulative_λ

Provenance and scope (2026-08-25). The witness named here is absent from the tree — added 2026-04-15 in commit e2814e577f under folio-assistant/computations/, lost in the miga migration. Recovered (analysis), its data.mass_by_level does carry 19 rows from H to ^{208}Pb, so the coverage claim below is fair, and its \mathrm{BW}(k{=}5) column is accurate (^3\mathrm{H} \to {}^3\mathrm{He}: 0.018228 against 0.01861 measured).

Its assertions are another matter. Seven of them test the inaccurate NF-trace column against experiment with a tolerance set just above each discrepancy — Q({}^3\mathrm{H} \to {}^3\mathrm{He}) is recorded as passing at 13\,017\% error under a tolerance 14\,319\% of the expected value. A bound sized to its own miss is a fit, and the owner directive of 2026-08-25 is no fitting. The contrast is inside the same file: B(\mathrm{T}) and B({}^3\mathrm{He}) carry tolerances of 0.0004 and 0.0001 and are recorded as failing at 0.0\% error.

Cite the \mathrm{BW}(k{=}5) figures if any; do not cite the NF-trace Q-values as confirmed.

Witness: mass-qvalue-by-level.witness.json — every isotope (^1H to ^{208}Pb), per-step rows recording per-partition contributions; restartable from any (A, Z_k, N_k, \{\ln|\mathrm{tr}|_\lambda\}, \mathrm{cumulative}).

See Table.

The unified path uses one symbolic algorithm with zero fitted parameters and no special-case branches. The discrepancy between the two paths quantifies the residual that the LP-dual accumulator over k \leq K_{\max} does not absorb; extending K_{\max} above 6 adds further partitions, with shadow prices and q-hooks computed by the same formulas.

Formal asymptotic content. The Féray–Méliot rate O(1/\sqrt{A}) has \ordw(\text{accumulator}) = -\tfrac{1}{2}\,\ordw(A) in the surreal valuation; see Big-O via \ordw and the body asymptotics catalog.
